title: Coupling Dy Triangles to Maximize the Toroidal Moment

material_class.structural_family: edge-to-edge Dy3+Dy3 hexanuclear cluster with μ4-O linkage

synthesis.procedure: Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (0.30 mmol) was reacted with the Schiff base H3L formed by in situ condensation of 2,6-diformyl-4-methylphenol (0.15 mmol) and ethanolamine (0.3 mmol) in 10 mL methanol in the presence of Et3N (0.45 mmol). The mixture was sealed in a reactor, heated to 90 °C for 3 days, and cooled slowly to room temperature to give yellow single crystals.
synthesis.temperature: 90 °C then cooled slowly to room temperature
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solvothermal reaction in a sealed reactor
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: slow cooling to room temperature yielded yellow single crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction

properties.summary: Hexanuclear Dy6 SMM formed by two edge-to-edge Dy3 triangles linked by μ4-O2−. Static magnetism indicates a non-magnetic (toroidal) ground doublet: χMT = 85.5 cm3 K mol−1 at 300 K (1 kOe), falling to 10.3 cm3 K mol−1 at 2.0 K, with a susceptibility maximum near 7 K under 1 kOe that is suppressed at 13 kOe. Magnetization at 1.9 K inflects near 9 kOe and reaches 32.9 μB at ~70 kOe without saturation. Micro-SQUID hysteresis at 0.03 K shows a step at Hc = ±0.95 T. Zero-field ac data show two relaxation processes with Ueff = 33.9 K (τ0 = 5.8×10−8 s, high-frequency) and 40.7 K (τ0 = 1.2×10−7 s, low-frequency). Ab initio/Ising analysis finds strongly axial Dy sites (gz ≈ 19.7–19.8) with tangential anisotropy axes, a first magnetic excited state at ~7.6–7.7 cm−1, and strong intra- and inter-triangle couplings that stabilize a large net toroidal moment.
